Sources:

[bukhari:1117] Sahih al-Bukhari 1117
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدَانُ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ طَهْمَانَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي الْحُسَيْنُ الْمُكْتِبُ، عَنِ ابْنِ بُرَيْدَةَ، عَنْ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ حُصَيْنٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ كَانَتْ بِي بَوَاسِيرُ فَسَأَلْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ صَلِّ قَائِمًا، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَسْتَطِعْ فَقَاعِدًا، فَإِنْ لَمْ تَسْتَطِعْ فَعَلَى جَنْبٍ ‏"‏‏.‏

[abudawud:701] Sunan Abi Dawud 701
Grading: Sahih (Al-Albani); Sahih (Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid); Sahih (Shuaib Al Arnaut)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا الْقَعْنَبِيُّ، عَنْ مَالِكٍ، عَنْ أَبِي النَّضْرِ، مَوْلَى عُمَرَ بْنِ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ بُسْرِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، أَنَّ زَيْدَ بْنَ خَالِدٍ الْجُهَنِيَّ، أَرْسَلَهُ إِلَى أَبِي جُهَيْمٍ يَسْأَلُهُ مَاذَا سَمِعَ مِنْ، رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي الْمَارِّ بَيْنَ يَدَىِ الْمُصَلِّي فَقَالَ أَبُو جُهَيْمٍ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الْمَارُّ بَيْنَ يَدَىِ الْمُصَلِّي مَاذَا عَلَيْهِ لَكَانَ أَنْ يَقِفَ أَرْبَعِينَ خَيْرٌ لَهُ مِنْ أَنْ يَمُرَّ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو النَّضْرِ لاَ أَدْرِي قَالَ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْمًا أَوْ شَهْرًا أَوْ سَنَةً ‏.‏

[ibnmajah:1223] Sunan Ibn Majah 1223
Grading: Sahih (Al-Albani); Sahih (Muhammad Fouad Abd al-Baqi); Sahih (Shuaib Al Arnaut)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا وَكِيعٌ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ طَهْمَانَ، عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ الْمُعَلِّمِ، عَنِ ابْنِ بُرَيْدَةَ، عَنْ عِمْرَانَ بْنِ حُصَيْنٍ، قَالَ كَانَ بِي النَّاصُورُ فَسَأَلْتُ النَّبِيَّ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ ‏ "‏ صَلِّ قَائِمًا. فَإِنْ لَمْ تَسْتَطِعْ فَقَاعِدًا. فَإِنْ لَمْ تَسْتَطِعْ، فَعَلَى جَنْبٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏

[bukhari:1000] Sahih al-Bukhari 1000
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا جُوَيْرِيَةُ بْنُ أَسْمَاءَ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، قَالَ كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يُصَلِّي فِي السَّفَرِ عَلَى رَاحِلَتِهِ، حَيْثُ تَوَجَّهَتْ بِهِ، يُومِئُ إِيمَاءً، صَلاَةَ اللَّيْلِ إِلاَّ الْفَرَائِضَ، وَيُوتِرُ عَلَى رَاحِلَتِهِ‏.‏

Question: my dad just had knee surgery and he can't stand up for salah. how is he supposed to pray?

He prays standing if he is able, and if he cannot, he prays sitting [bukhari:1117]. The Prophet ﷺ gave this guidance to Imran bin Husain, who was suffering from an illness, and added that if sitting is also not possible, the prayer is done lying on one's side [bukhari:1117]. Ibn Majah records the same instruction from Imran: standing, then sitting, then on the side, and it is graded Sahih [ibnmajah:1223]. So your father's inability to stand does not remove the prayer from him; he moves to the next position he is able to manage [ibnmajah:1223].

[bukhari:4297] Sahih al-Bukhari 4297
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو نُعَيْمٍ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ،‏.‏ حَدَّثَنَا قَبِيصَةُ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ أَنَسٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ أَقَمْنَا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَشْرًا نَقْصُرُ الصَّلاَةَ‏.‏

[abudawud:157] Sunan Abi Dawud 157
Grading: Sahih (Al-Albani); Sahih (Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid); Sahih (Shuaib Al Arnaut)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا حَفْصُ بْنُ عُمَرَ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنِ الْحَكَمِ، وَحَمَّادٍ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْجَدَلِيِّ، عَنْ خُزَيْمَةَ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ الْمَسْحُ عَلَى الْخُفَّيْنِ لِلْمُسَافِرِ ثَلاَثَةُ أَيَّامٍ وَلِلْمُقِيمِ يَوْمٌ وَلَيْلَةٌ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو دَاوُدَ رَوَاهُ مَنْصُورُ بْنُ الْمُعْتَمِرِ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ التَّيْمِيِّ بِإِسْنَادِهِ قَالَ فِيهِ وَلَوِ اسْتَزَدْنَاهُ لَزَادَنَا ‏.‏

[bukhari:4299] Sahih al-Bukhari 4299
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ يُونُسَ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو شِهَابٍ، عَنْ عَاصِمٍ، عَنْ عِكْرِمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ أَقَمْنَا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي سَفَرٍ تِسْعَ عَشْرَةَ نَقْصُرُ الصَّلاَةَ‏.‏ وَقَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ وَنَحْنُ نَقْصُرُ مَا بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ تِسْعَ عَشْرَةَ، فَإِذَا زِدْنَا أَتْمَمْنَا‏.‏

[muslim:1688] Sahih Muslim 1688 (Abd al-Baqi no. 725a)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عُبَيْدٍ الْغُبَرِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو عَوَانَةَ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، عَنْ زُرَارَةَ بْنِ أَوْفَى، عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ هِشَامٍ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ رَكْعَتَا الْفَجْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا وَمَا فِيهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏

Question: How many days can I keep shortening my prayers if I'm staying in another city for a while?

The narrations give different lengths of stay. Anas reported that they stayed in Makkah with the Prophet ﷺ for ten days and kept offering the shortened prayers [bukhari:4297]. Ibn Abbas reported a journey on which they stayed nineteen days while shortening, and his own practice was to shorten for a stay of up to nineteen days and to pray in full if the stay was longer [bukhari:4299]. Because these reports describe different stays, people have understood the limit differently, and the sources here do not settle a single fixed number. Please ask a qualified scholar which view to follow for your situation.

[abudawud:1201] Sunan Abi Dawud 1201
Grading: Sahih (Al-Albani); Sahih (Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid); Sahih Muslim (691) (Zubair Ali Zai)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ بَشَّارٍ، حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ يَزِيدَ الْهُنَائِيِّ، قَالَ سَأَلْتُ أَنَسَ بْنَ مَالِكٍ عَنْ قَصْرِ الصَّلاَةِ، فَقَالَ أَنَسٌ كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا خَرَجَ مَسِيرَةَ ثَلاَثَةِ أَمْيَالٍ أَوْ ثَلاَثَةِ فَرَاسِخَ - شُعْبَةُ شَكَّ - يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ ‏.‏

[malik:337] Muwatta Malik 337
Grading: Mauquf Sahih (Salim al-Hilali)
(ar) وَحَدَّثَنِي عَنْ مَالِكٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ، عَنْ سَالِمِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّهُ رَكِبَ إِلَى رِيمٍ فَقَصَرَ الصَّلاَةَ فِي مَسِيرِهِ ذَلِكَ ‏.‏ قَالَ مَالِكٌ وَذَلِكَ نَحْوٌ مِنْ أَرْبَعَةِ بُرُدٍ ‏.‏

Question: what's the minimum distance of travel before you're allowed to do qasr?

The reports point in different directions. Anas was asked about shortening the prayer and said that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out on a journey of three miles or three farsakh, he prayed two rak'ahs, with the narrator Shu'bah unsure which of the two was said [abudawud:1201]. In the Muwatta, Ibn Umar shortened the prayer when he rode to a place called Rim, and Malik said that was about four mail-stages [malik:337]. So one report links shortening to a short trip while the other reflects a much longer distance. A qualified scholar can tell you which position to act on.

[nasai:128] Sunan an-Nasa'i 128
Grading: Sahih (Abu Ghuddah); Sahih (Al-Albani); Sahih Muslim (Zubair Ali Zai)
(ar) أَخْبَرَنَا إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ أَنْبَأَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، قَالَ أَنْبَأَنَا الثَّوْرِيُّ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ قَيْسٍ الْمُلاَئِيِّ، عَنِ الْحَكَمِ بْنِ عُتَيْبَةَ، عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُخَيْمِرَةَ، عَنْ شُرَيْحِ بْنِ هَانِئٍ، عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، - رضى الله عنه - قَالَ جَعَلَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لِلْمُسَافِرِ ثَلاَثَةَ أَيَّامٍ وَلَيَالِيَهُنَّ وَيَوْمًا وَلَيْلَةً لِلْمُقِيمِ يَعْنِي فِي الْمَسْحِ ‏.‏

[abudawud:327] Sunan Abi Dawud 327
Grading: Sahih (Al-Albani); Sahih (Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid); Hasan (Zubair Ali Zai)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْمِنْهَالِ، حَدَّثَنَا يَزِيدُ بْنُ زُرَيْعٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدٍ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ، عَنْ عَزْرَةَ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبْزَى، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ يَاسِرٍ، قَالَ سَأَلْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عَنِ التَّيَمُّمِ فَأَمَرَنِي ضَرْبَةً وَاحِدَةً لِلْوَجْهِ وَالْكَفَّيْنِ ‏.‏

Question: How do you actually do tayammum?

The Prophet ﷺ struck the earth with his hands and then wiped his face and the backs of his hands with them [bukhari:343]. Ammar reported that he was told to strike the ground once for the face and the hands [abudawud:327].

Grading: Sahih (Al-Albani); Sahih (Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid); Sahih Bukhari (751) (Zubair Ali Zai)

Question: Which sunnah prayers go with the five daily prayers and what's the reward?

Ibn Umar remembered ten rak'ahs from the Prophet ﷺ: two before Zuhr and two after it, two after Maghrib at home, two after Isha at home, and two before Fajr [bukhari:1180]. Umm Habibah reported that whoever prays twelve rak'ahs in a day will have a house built for him in Paradise [nasai:1810]. The two rak'ahs before dawn have a special place: the Prophet ﷺ said they are better than this world and everything in it [muslim:1688].

Question: I always lose count in salah, was it 3 rakat or 4?? what do I do

When you are unsure how many rak'ahs you have prayed, set the doubt aside and build on what you are certain of, then make two prostrations before finishing [abudawud:1024]. In that narration the Prophet ﷺ explained that if the prayer was already complete, the extra rak'ah and the two prostrations count as voluntary, and if it was short, they make it up, while the prostrations humiliate the devil [abudawud:1024]. He also said that Satan comes to the one praying and confuses him until he forgets how many rak'ahs he has prayed, and that such a person should make two prostrations of forgetfulness while sitting [bukhari:1232].

Question: Is ghusl on Friday actually obligatory or is wudu enough for jummah?

The narrations differ in wording. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reported that the Prophet ﷺ said bathing on Friday is compulsory for every Muslim who has reached puberty [bukhari:858]. Anas reported that whoever performs ablution on Friday has done well and fulfilled what is required, but bathing is better [ibnmajah:1091]. Samurah's narration also says that ablution on Friday is fine and a bath is better, and it is graded Hasan [abudawud:354]. Because one wording sounds obligatory and the others describe the bath as better, scholars have read them differently, so it is best to ask a qualified scholar for a ruling.

Question: is it wrong to tell someone to be quiet during the jumuah khutbah?

Yes, the Prophet ﷺ said that if you tell your companion to keep quiet and listen while the imam is delivering the khutbah, you have done something wrong yourself [bukhari:934]. In the wording recorded by an-Nasa'i, telling your companion to be quiet and listen during the khutbah is counted as idle speech [nasai:1577].

Question: How can I stop my mind and eyes wandering in prayer, is looking around a big deal?

Allah says: "Be guardians of your prayers, and of the midmost prayer, and stand up with devotion to Allah" [quran:2:238]. The Prophet ﷺ spoke sternly about people who look up at the sky during prayer and warned that they should stop or their sight would be taken away [bukhari:750]. When Aishah asked him about looking to the sides during prayer, he said it is something the devil snatches from a servant's prayer [abudawud:910]. The Quran also reminds that worship preserves from lewdness and that remembrance of Allah is greater [quran:29:45].

Question: how long can you wipe over khuffs before you have to take them off and wash your feet?

The Prophet ﷺ set the limit at three days and nights for a traveller and one day and night for a resident [abudawud:157]. Tirmidhi records the same answer when he was asked about wiping over the khuff: three for the traveller and one day for the resident [tirmidhi:95].

Question: When does each prayer time start and end according to hadith?

The Quran says that worship at fixed times has been enjoined on the believers [quran:4:103]. When a man asked the Prophet ﷺ about the times, he prayed Zuhr after the sun passed its zenith, Asr when a thing's shadow equalled its height, Maghrib at sunset and Isha when the twilight had gone; on the next day he prayed Zuhr when a man's shadow equalled his height, Asr when it was twice his height, and Maghrib just before the twilight disappeared, with Isha up to a third of the night [nasai:504]. Ibn Abbas reported that Jibril led the Prophet ﷺ twice at the House, praying Fajr when dawn began, and Maghrib when the sun had set and the fasting person breaks the fast [tirmidhi:149].

Question: Can I pray with my shoes on? and is it ok on the carpet in the masjid?

Praying in shoes has a basis: Anas was asked whether the Prophet ﷺ ever prayed with his shoes on, and he answered yes [bukhari:386]. Abdullah ibn as-Sa'ib also saw him praying on the day of the conquest of Makkah with his shoe placed on his left side [abudawud:648]. I'm not sure about wearing shoes on a carpeted masjid floor today, because these sources do not discuss that; please follow the mosque's rules and ask a local imam.

Question: are the 2 sunnah before fajr really that important?

Yes, the Prophet ﷺ said that the two rak'ahs at dawn are better than this world and what it contains [muslim:1688]. Ibn Umar also counted them among the voluntary prayers the Prophet ﷺ kept, offered before the Fajr prayer [bukhari:1180].

Question: On a long train ride can I pray my fard prayers sitting in my seat facing whatever way the train goes?

For voluntary prayers there is clear precedent: the Prophet ﷺ prayed nawafil on his mount facing whichever way it was going, using gestures, and he also prayed witr on it, but he did not pray the compulsory prayers that way [bukhari:1000]. Tirmidhi also reports that he prayed on his mount whichever direction it faced [tirmidhi:352]. I'm not sure how this applies to obligatory prayers on a modern train, since these reports exclude the compulsory prayer and do not discuss trains; please ask a qualified scholar.

Question: How bad is it to walk in front of someone praying, and how far in front is ok?

It is serious: the Prophet ﷺ said that if the one who passes in front of a praying man knew what he takes upon himself, he would prefer to stand still for forty rather than pass, and the narrator Abu al-Nadr did not know whether forty days, months or years was meant [abudawud:701]. I'm not sure about how much distance in front of the person makes passing acceptable, as this source does not specify it.

Question: Is it better to eat suhoor late and break the fast right at maghrib or does timing not matter?

Suhoor itself is encouraged: the Prophet ﷺ said to eat it, because there is blessing in it [nasai:2150]. For breaking the fast, he said the people will remain upon goodness as long as they hasten to break their fast [tirmidhi:699]. Abu Hurairah's narration adds the instruction to hasten the iftar, noting that the Jews delay it, and it is graded Hasan Sahih [ibnmajah:1698]. So the sources favour taking suhoor and not delaying the iftar once its time has come.

Question: what did the prophet break his fast with?? dates only?

Anas reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ broke his fast with fresh dates before praying, and if there were none, with dried dates, and if there were no dried dates, he took a few sips of water [tirmidhi:696]. A narration from Salman ibn Amir instructs the fasting person to break the fast with dates, or with water if dates cannot be found because water is purifying, but it is graded Da'if [abudawud:2355]. Another narration from Anas with a similar instruction about dried dates and water is also graded Da'if [tirmidhi:694]. The authentic report describes his practice rather than a strict rule of dates only.

(ar) أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيَامِ الرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَائِكُمْ ۚ هُنَّ لِبَاسٌ لَكُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ لِبَاسٌ لَهُنَّ ۗ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَخْتَانُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَعَفَا عَنْكُمْ ۖ فَالْآنَ بَاشِرُوهُنَّ وَابْتَغُوا مَا كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۚ وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ ۖ ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا الصِّيَامَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ ۚ وَلَا تُبَاشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنْتُمْ عَاكِفُونَ فِي الْمَسَاجِدِ ۗ تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ فَلَا تَقْرَبُوهَا ۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ آيَاتِهِ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ
(en) It is made lawful for you to go in unto your wives on the night of the fast. They are raiment for you and ye are raiment for them. Allah is Aware that ye were deceiving yourselves in this respect and He hath turned in mercy toward you and relieved you. So hold intercourse with them and seek that which Allah hath ordained for you, and eat and drink until the white thread becometh distinct to you from the black thread of the dawn. Then strictly observe the fast till nightfall and touch them not, but be at your devotions in the mosques. These are the limits imposed by Allah, so approach them not. Thus Allah expoundeth His revelation to mankind that they may ward off (evil)

[abudawud:2385] Sunan Abi Dawud 2385
Grading: Sahih (Al-Albani); Sahih (Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid); Sahih (Shuaib Al Arnaut)

Question: Can a husband kiss his wife while fasting in Ramadan?

The narrations show different considerations. Aishah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kissed and embraced while fasting, but that he had the greatest control over his desire [muslim:2576]. When Umar kissed while fasting and was worried, the Prophet ﷺ compared it to rinsing the mouth with water while fasting [abudawud:2385]. On the other hand, Abu Hurairah reported that he allowed an old man to embrace while fasting but forbade a young man [abudawud:2387]. Because of these differences, scholars weigh a person's self-control differently, so please ask a qualified scholar about your own case.

Question: whats the reward for fasting 6 days of shawwal?

The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever fasts Ramadan and then follows it with six days in Shawwal, it is like a perpetual fast [abudawud:2433]. In Tirmidhi's wording from the same Companion, Abu Ayyub, fasting Ramadan and then six days of Shawwal is equal in reward to fasting every day [tirmidhi:759].

Question: Is fasting on the day of Arafah worth it if I'm not doing hajj?

The Prophet ﷺ said that he hoped fasting on the Day of Arafah would expiate the sins of the year before and the year after [ibnmajah:1730]. A similar narration from Qatadah bin Nu'man promising forgiveness of the previous and following year is graded Da'if by Al-Albani, so the first, authentic narration is the one to rely on [ibnmajah:1731].

Question: Someone told me fasting only on a Friday is not allowed, is that true?

Yes, Abu Hurairah heard the Prophet ﷺ say that none of you should fast on Friday unless he fasts a day before it or after it [bukhari:1985]. Ibn Majah reports that he forbade fasting on a Friday unless it is joined to the day before or the day after [ibnmajah:1723]. Abu Dawud records the same instruction [abudawud:2420]. So the concern is singling out Friday on its own, not fasting it together with a neighbouring day.

Question: My grandfather passed away and he had missed some Ramadan fasts. Do we fast for him or feed poor people?

The reports differ. Aishah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said whoever dies while owing fasts, his guardians should fast on his behalf [bukhari:1952]. Ibn Abbas held that if a man fell ill in Ramadan and died without being able to fast, food is given on his behalf, while a vow he could not fulfil is made up by his heir [abudawud:2401]. A narration that whoever dies owing a month of fasts should have a poor person fed for each day is graded Da'if [ibnmajah:1757]. Since these point to different practices, please ask a qualified scholar which applies to your grandfather.

Question: i threw up while fasting today, it just happened, is my fast gone?

The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever is overcome by vomiting does not have to make up the fast, while whoever vomits on purpose must make it up [tirmidhi:720]. Ibn Majah records the same distinction between unintentional and deliberate vomiting [ibnmajah:1676]. Abdullah ibn Umar also used to say that someone who makes himself vomit while fasting makes up a day, but not someone who could not help it [malik:677]. So if it was not deliberate, these sources say you do not need to make up the day.

Aishah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ practised i'tikaf in the last ten nights of Ramadan and told people to look for the Night of Qadr in those last ten nights [bukhari:2020]. Tirmidhi records the same from her: he stayed in i'tikaf during the last ten and said to seek the Night of Al-Qadr in them [tirmidhi:792]. So the timing is tied to seeking that night.

Question: I want to fast Ashura. Do I fast only the 10th, and what's the reward? Also is it ok to fast the 11th instead of the 9th?

The Prophet ﷺ said he anticipated that fasting the Day of Ashura would bring forgiveness for the year before it [tirmidhi:752]. Ibn Abbas reported that he said that if he lived until the next year he would fast the ninth as well [muslim:2667]. I'm not sure about fasting the 11th in place of the 9th, because these sources only mention the ninth; a qualified scholar can advise you.

(ar) حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ دَاوُدَ الْمَهْرِيُّ، أَخْبَرَنَا ابْنُ وَهْبٍ، أَخْبَرَنِي جَرِيرُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ، وَسَمَّى، آخَرَ عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ ضَمْرَةَ، وَالْحَارِثِ الأَعْوَرِ، عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، - رضى الله عنه - عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِبَعْضِ أَوَّلِ هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِذَا كَانَتْ لَكَ مِائَتَا دِرْهَمٍ وَحَالَ عَلَيْهَا الْحَوْلُ فَفِيهَا خَمْسَةُ دَرَاهِمَ وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ شَىْءٌ - يَعْنِي فِي الذَّهَبِ - حَتَّى يَكُونَ لَكَ عِشْرُونَ دِينَارًا فَإِذَا كَانَ لَكَ عِشْرُونَ دِينَارًا وَحَالَ عَلَيْهَا الْحَوْلُ فَفِيهَا نِصْفُ دِينَارٍ فَمَا زَادَ فَبِحِسَابِ ذَلِكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَعَلِيٌّ يَقُولُ فَبِحِسَابِ ذَلِكَ ‏.‏ أَوْ رَفَعَهُ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ وَلَيْسَ فِي مَالٍ زَكَاةٌ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ إِلاَّ أَنَّ جَرِيرًا قَالَ ابْنُ وَهْبٍ يَزِيدُ فِي الْحَدِيثِ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لَيْسَ فِي مَالٍ زَكَاةٌ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏

[bukhari:1459] Sahih al-Bukhari 1459
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ يُوسُفَ، أَخْبَرَنَا مَالِكٌ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي صَعْصَعَةَ الْمَازِنِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏ "‏ لَيْسَ فِيمَا دُونَ خَمْسَةِ أَوْسُقٍ مِنَ التَّمْرِ صَدَقَةٌ، وَلَيْسَ فِيمَا دُونَ خَمْسِ أَوَاقٍ مِنَ الْوَرِقِ صَدَقَةٌ، وَلَيْسَ فِيمَا دُونَ خَمْسِ ذَوْدٍ مِنَ الإِبِلِ صَدَقَةٌ ‏"‏‏.‏

Question: How much gold or silver do I need to own before zakat is due, and how much do I pay?

The Prophet ﷺ said that when you possess two hundred dirhams and a year passes on them, five dirhams are due, and nothing is due on gold until it reaches twenty dinars, at which point half a dinar is due after a year [abudawud:1573]. The same narration says no zakat is payable on property until a year has passed on it [abudawud:1573]. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri also reported that there is no zakat on less than five awaq of silver, five camels, or five awsuq of dates [bukhari:1459].

Question: Do women have to pay zakat on the gold jewellery they actually wear?

The sources show two positions. In a narration graded Hasan, two women came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wearing gold bracelets; he asked whether they had paid their zakat, warned them about bracelets of Fire, and told them to pay it [tirmidhi:637]. In the Muwatta, Abdullah ibn Umar adorned his daughters with gold jewellery and did not take zakat from it, and Malik said zakat is paid on jewellery only when it is kept for purposes other than wearing [malik:588]. Since these differ, please ask a qualified scholar which view to follow.

Question: how much zakat on crops like wheat?

The Prophet ﷺ said that crops watered by rain and springs owe one-tenth, and those irrigated by watering owe half of one-tenth [ibnmajah:1816]. Ibn Umar's narration in Bukhari likewise sets one-tenth for land watered by rain or natural channels and half of that for irrigated land [bukhari:1483].

(ar) حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ بَشَّارٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَهَّابِ الثَّقَفِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا أَيُّوبُ، عَنْ نَافِعٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ، قَالَ مَنِ اسْتَفَادَ مَالاً فَلاَ زَكَاةَ فِيهِ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو عِيسَى وَهَذَا أَصَحُّ مِنْ حَدِيثِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو عِيسَى وَرَوَى أَيُّوبُ وَعُبَيْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ وَغَيْرُ وَاحِدٍ عَنْ نَافِعٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ مَوْقُوفًا ‏.‏ وَعَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ ضَعِيفٌ فِي الْحَدِيثِ ضَعَّفَهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ حَنْبَلٍ وَعَلِيُّ بْنُ الْمَدِينِيِّ وَغَيْرُهُمَا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْحَدِيثِ وَهُوَ كَثِيرُ الْغَلَطِ ‏.‏ وَقَدْ رُوِيَ عَنْ غَيْرِ وَاحِدٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنْ لاَ زَكَاةَ فِي الْمَالِ الْمُسْتَفَادِ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ ‏.‏ وَبِهِ يَقُولُ مَالِكُ بْنُ أَنَسٍ وَالشَّافِعِيُّ وَأَحْمَدُ وَإِسْحَاقُ ‏.‏ وَقَالَ بَعْضُ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ إِذَا كَانَ عِنْدَهُ مَالٌ تَجِبُ فِيهِ الزَّكَاةُ فَفِيهِ الزَّكَاةُ وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ عِنْدَهُ سِوَى الْمَالِ الْمُسْتَفَادِ مَا تَجِبُ فِيهِ الزَّكَاةُ لَمْ يَجِبْ عَلَيْهِ فِي الْمَالِ الْمُسْتَفَادِ زَكَاةٌ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ فَإِنِ اسْتَفَادَ مَ …

[abudawud:1573] Sunan Abi Dawud 1573
Grading: Sahih (Al-Albani); Sahih (Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid); Daif (Zubair Ali Zai)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ دَاوُدَ الْمَهْرِيُّ، أَخْبَرَنَا ابْنُ وَهْبٍ، أَخْبَرَنِي جَرِيرُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ، وَسَمَّى، آخَرَ عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ ضَمْرَةَ، وَالْحَارِثِ الأَعْوَرِ، عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، - رضى الله عنه - عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِبَعْضِ أَوَّلِ هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِذَا كَانَتْ لَكَ مِائَتَا دِرْهَمٍ وَحَالَ عَلَيْهَا الْحَوْلُ فَفِيهَا خَمْسَةُ دَرَاهِمَ وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ شَىْءٌ - يَعْنِي فِي الذَّهَبِ - حَتَّى يَكُونَ لَكَ عِشْرُونَ دِينَارًا فَإِذَا كَانَ لَكَ عِشْرُونَ دِينَارًا وَحَالَ عَلَيْهَا الْحَوْلُ فَفِيهَا نِصْفُ دِينَارٍ فَمَا زَادَ فَبِحِسَابِ ذَلِكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَعَلِيٌّ يَقُولُ فَبِحِسَابِ ذَلِكَ ‏.‏ أَوْ رَفَعَهُ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ وَلَيْسَ فِي مَالٍ زَكَاةٌ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ إِلاَّ أَنَّ جَرِيرًا قَالَ ابْنُ وَهْبٍ يَزِيدُ فِي الْحَدِيثِ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لَيْسَ فِي مَالٍ زَكَاةٌ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏

Question: I got a big bonus last month, do I need to pay zakat on it right away?

Aishah heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say that there is no zakat on wealth until a full year has passed over it [ibnmajah:1792]. Ibn Umar said the same about newly acquired wealth: no zakat is due on it until the year has passed while it is in the owner's possession [tirmidhi:632]. Ali's narration also links zakat on two hundred dirhams to a year passing over them [abudawud:1573]. So according to these sources the bonus becomes zakatable once a year has passed on it.

Question: What kind of charity is the best one to give?

When asked which charity is best, the Prophet ﷺ said it is giving while you are healthy, eager for wealth, hoping to become rich and fearing poverty, and not delaying until you are on your deathbed handing out shares when the property already belongs to your heirs [bukhari:2748]. He also said from the pulpit that the upper hand is better than the lower hand, the upper being the one who gives [bukhari:1429]. The Quran adds: "Spend of the good things which ye have earned" and do not seek out the bad to give away [quran:2:267].

Question: Does giving sadaqah to my own brother who is struggling count, or should it go to strangers?

Giving to a relative counts and is rewarded twice: the Prophet ﷺ said that charity to a poor person is charity, while charity to a relative is two things, charity and upholding the ties of kinship [nasai:2582]. When Zainab, the wife of Abdullah, asked whether spending on her husband and the orphans in her care was accepted as charity, he said she would have two rewards, for charity and for kinship [ibnmajah:1834].

(ar) إِنْ تُبْدُوا الصَّدَقَاتِ فَنِعِمَّا هِيَ ۖ وَإِنْ تُخْفُوهَا وَتُؤْتُوهَا الْفُقَرَاءَ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ ۚ وَيُكَفِّرُ عَنْكُمْ مِنْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ
(en) If ye publish your almsgiving, it is well, but if ye hide it and give it to the poor, it will be better for you, and will atone for some of your ill-deeds. Allah is Informed of what ye do

[bukhari:2760] Sahih al-Bukhari 2760
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي مَالِكٌ، عَنْ هِشَامٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، رضى الله عنها أَنَّ رَجُلاً، قَالَ لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِنَّ أُمِّي افْتُلِتَتْ نَفْسَهَا، وَأُرَاهَا لَوْ تَكَلَّمَتْ تَصَدَّقَتْ، أَفَأَتَصَدَّقُ عَنْهَا قَالَ ‏ "‏ نَعَمْ، تَصَدَّقْ عَنْهَا ‏"‏‏.‏

Question: My mother died last year without leaving a will. Can I give charity for her and will she get the reward?

Yes. A man told the Prophet ﷺ that his mother had died suddenly and that he thought she would have given charity had she been able to speak, and asked if he could give on her behalf; the Prophet ﷺ said yes [bukhari:2760]. In another narration from Ibn Abbas, a man asked whether it would benefit his deceased mother if he gave charity for her, and the Prophet ﷺ said yes, after which the man gave his garden in charity for her [tirmidhi:669].

Question: is it better to donate publicly to encourage others or in secret?

The Quran says: "If ye publish your almsgiving, it is well, but if ye hide it and give it to the poor, it will be better for you, and will atone for some of your ill-deeds" [quran:2:271]. Whichever way you give, the Quran warns: "Render not vain your almsgiving by reproach and injury, like him who spendeth his wealth only to be seen of men" [quran:2:264]. Those who spend for Allah's cause and do not follow it with reproach or injury have their reward with their Lord [quran:2:262].

(ar) حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ دَاوُدَ الْمَهْرِيُّ، أَخْبَرَنَا ابْنُ وَهْبٍ، أَخْبَرَنِي جَرِيرُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ، وَسَمَّى، آخَرَ عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ، عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ ضَمْرَةَ، وَالْحَارِثِ الأَعْوَرِ، عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، - رضى الله عنه - عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِبَعْضِ أَوَّلِ هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِذَا كَانَتْ لَكَ مِائَتَا دِرْهَمٍ وَحَالَ عَلَيْهَا الْحَوْلُ فَفِيهَا خَمْسَةُ دَرَاهِمَ وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ شَىْءٌ - يَعْنِي فِي الذَّهَبِ - حَتَّى يَكُونَ لَكَ عِشْرُونَ دِينَارًا فَإِذَا كَانَ لَكَ عِشْرُونَ دِينَارًا وَحَالَ عَلَيْهَا الْحَوْلُ فَفِيهَا نِصْفُ دِينَارٍ فَمَا زَادَ فَبِحِسَابِ ذَلِكَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَلاَ أَدْرِي أَعَلِيٌّ يَقُولُ فَبِحِسَابِ ذَلِكَ ‏.‏ أَوْ رَفَعَهُ إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ وَلَيْسَ فِي مَالٍ زَكَاةٌ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ إِلاَّ أَنَّ جَرِيرًا قَالَ ابْنُ وَهْبٍ يَزِيدُ فِي الْحَدِيثِ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لَيْسَ فِي مَالٍ زَكَاةٌ حَتَّى يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ ‏"‏ ‏.‏

Question: Can my wife give food from our house to the poor without asking me each time? Is there a limit?

The Prophet ﷺ said that if a woman gives food in charity from her husband's house without spoiling his property, she gets a reward and her husband gets a similar reward, he for earning it and she for spending it [bukhari:1440]. I'm not sure about a fixed limit or whether permission is needed each time, because this source does not set either; a qualified scholar can advise you.

Question: Do I owe zakat on my gold and on my car?

For gold, the Prophet ﷺ said nothing is due until it reaches twenty dinars, and when you own twenty dinars for a full year, half a dinar is due [abudawud:1573]. Silver has a threshold too: there is no zakat on less than five awaq [bukhari:1459]. I'm not sure about the car, because these sources do not mention vehicles or personal-use items; please ask a qualified scholar.

Question: What can't a man wear once he's in ihram?

When asked what a muhrim should wear, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said he should not wear a shirt, turbans, trousers, a hooded cloak, or a garment perfumed with saffron or wars, and that if sandals are not available he may wear khuffs cut so that they come below the ankles [bukhari:1842]. Muslim records the same answer from Ibn Umar, listing the shirt, turban, cap and trousers among what the muhrim does not wear [muslim:2792].

Question: Is it true that umrah in ramadan is like doing hajj?

Yes, Umm Ma'qil narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said umrah during Ramadan is equal to Hajj [tirmidhi:939]. Ibn Abbas reported that he told a woman from the Ansar to perform umrah when Ramadan came, because umrah in that month is equivalent to Hajj [nasai:2110]. These narrations speak of its reward being equal; they do not say it replaces the obligation of Hajj.

Question: what does a hajj without sins get you

The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever performs Hajj to this House without sexual relations or disobedience will go back like the day his mother bore him [ibnmajah:2889]. An-Nasa'i records the same promise for the one who avoids obscenity and sin on the pilgrimage [nasai:2627]. The Quran sets the same standard: "there is (to be) no lewdness nor abuse nor angry conversation on the pilgrimage" [quran:2:197].

Question: What's the single most important part of hajj?

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said three times that the Hajj is Arafat, and that whoever attends Arafah before the rising of Fajr has performed the Hajj [tirmidhi:2975]. In the same narration he mentioned that the days of Mina are three, with no sin on one who leaves after two [tirmidhi:2975].

Question: My father is too old and weak to travel. Can I do Hajj for him?

Yes. A woman from Khath'am told the Prophet ﷺ that Hajj had become due on her father but he was very old and could not sit on his mount, and asked whether it would count if she performed it for him; he answered yes [bukhari:1853]. A man from Banu Amir also said his father was very old and could not perform Hajj or umrah or ride, and the Prophet ﷺ told him to perform Hajj and umrah on his father's behalf [abudawud:1810].

Question: How far can a woman travel without a mahram? I've heard different numbers.

The narrations mention different lengths. Ibn Umar reported that the Prophet ﷺ said a woman should not travel for more than three days except with a mahram [bukhari:1087]. Abu Hurairah reported that it is not permissible for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to travel one day and night except with a mahram [bukhari:1088]. Another wording from Abu Hurairah speaks of more than one day's distance [ibnmajah:2899]. Because the reported durations differ, scholars have reached different conclusions, so please ask a qualified scholar for a ruling on your situation.

Question: My period might start during hajj. What can I still do and what do I have to skip?

Aishah was menstruating when she reached Makkah, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ told her to perform all the ceremonies of Hajj like the other pilgrims but not to do tawaf of the Ka'bah until she became clean [bukhari:1650]. Ibn Abbas also reported that people were ordered to make the farewell tawaf their last act before leaving, except menstruating women, who were excused from it [bukhari:1755].

Question: after umrah is it better to shave the head or just trim?

Both are valid, but shaving was given more emphasis: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed for mercy on those who shaved their heads, and only when the people asked repeatedly did he include those who cut their hair short [bukhari:1727]. Ibn Majah records the same exchange from Ibn Umar, with the prayer for those who shave coming first [ibnmajah:3044].

Question: is there a hadith about drinking zamzam with an intention?

Yes, Jabir bin Abdullah heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say that the water of Zamzam is for whatever it is drunk for [ibnmajah:3062]. This narration in Ibn Majah is graded Sahih by Al-Albani, so it can be relied on [ibnmajah:3062].

Question: What are the words of the talbiyah the Prophet used?

Ibn Umar reported the Prophet's talbiyah as: labbayk Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wa an-ni'mata laka wa al-mulk, la sharika lak [abudawud:1812]. Nafi said that Ibn Umar kept to these same words in his own talbiyah [tirmidhi:826].

Question: What dua do I say after the adhan finishes and what's the reward?

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that whoever, on hearing the call to prayer, asks Allah, the Lord of this perfect call and of the established prayer, to grant Muhammad the wasilah and excellence and to raise him to the praiseworthy station He promised, will be assured of his intercession [abudawud:529]. Tirmidhi records the same supplication from Jabir bin Abdullah, beginning Allahumma rabba hadhihi ad-da'wati at-tammah [tirmidhi:211].

Question: what to say before going into the bathroom

Anas reported that whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the toilet he would say: Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min al-khubuthi wal-khaba'ith, seeking refuge with Allah from the male and female devils [nasai:19]. Ibn Majah records the same practice from Anas, with the slightly different wording a'udhu billahi min al-khubthi wal-khaba'ith, which is also graded Sahih [ibnmajah:298].

(ar) حَدَّثَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ يُونُسَ، حَدَّثَنَا زُهَيْرٌ، حَدَّثَنَا عُبَيْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْمَقْبُرِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ إِذَا أَوَى أَحَدُكُمْ إِلَى فِرَاشِهِ فَلْيَنْفُضْ فِرَاشَهُ بِدَاخِلَةِ إِزَارِهِ فَإِنَّهُ لاَ يَدْرِي مَا خَلَفَهُ عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ لْيَضْطَجِعْ عَلَى شِقِّهِ الأَيْمَنِ ثُمَّ لْيَقُلْ بِاسْمِكَ رَبِّي وَضَعْتُ جَنْبِي وَبِكَ أَرْفَعُهُ إِنْ أَمْسَكْتَ نَفْسِي فَارْحَمْهَا وَإِنْ أَرْسَلْتَهَا فَاحْفَظْهَا بِمَا تَحْفَظُ بِهِ عِبَادَكَ الصَّالِحِينَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏

[tirmidhi:3574] Jami at-Tirmidhi 3574
Grading: Sahih (Ahmad Muhammad Shakir); Sahih (Al-Albani); Hasan Sahih (Bashar Awad Maarouf)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ بْنُ وَكِيعٍ، حَدَّثَنَا جَرِيرٌ، عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ، عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ عُبَيْدَةَ، حَدَّثَنِي الْبَرَاءُ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ إِذَا أَخَذْتَ مَضْجَعَكَ فَتَوَضَّأْ وُضُوءَكَ لِلصَّلاَةِ ثُمَّ اضْطَجِعْ عَلَى شِقِّكَ الأَيْمَنِ ثُمَّ قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِي إِلَيْكَ وَفَوَّضْتُ أَمْرِي إِلَيْكَ وَأَلْجَأْتُ ظَهْرِي إِلَيْكَ رَهْبَةً وَرَغْبَةً إِلَيْكَ لاَ مَلْجَأَ وَلاَ مَنْجَا مِنْكَ إِلاَّ إِلَيْكَ آمَنْتُ بِكِتَابِكَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلْتَ وَبِنَبِيِّكَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلْتَ ‏.‏ فَإِنْ مُتَّ فِي لَيْلَتِكَ مُتَّ عَلَى الْفِطْرَةِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَرَدَّدْتُهُنَّ لأَسْتَذْكِرَهُ فَقُلْتُ آمَنْتُ بِرَسُولِكَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلْتَ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِنَبِيِّكَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلْتَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ وَهَذَا حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ صَحِيحٌ ‏.‏ وَقَدْ رُوِيَ مِنْ غَيْرِ وَجْهٍ عَنِ الْبَرَاءِ وَلاَ نَعْلَمُ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنَ الرِّوَايَاتِ ذُكِرَ الْوُضُوءُ إِلاَّ فِي هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ ‏.‏

[bukhari:6345] Sahih al-Bukhari 6345
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا مُسْلِمُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، حَدَّثَنَا هِشَامٌ، حَدَّثَنَا قَتَادَةُ، عَنْ أَبِي الْعَالِيَةِ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَدْعُو عِنْدَ الْكَرْبِ ‏ "‏ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ الْعَظِيمُ الْحَلِيمُ، لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ رَبُّ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ، رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ ‏"‏‏.‏

[muslim:1352] Sahih Muslim 1352 (Abd al-Baqi no. 597a)
(ar) حَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ الْحَمِيدِ بْنُ بَيَانٍ الْوَاسِطِيُّ، أَخْبَرَنَا خَالِدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ سُهَيْلٍ، عَنْ أَبِي عُبَيْدٍ الْمَذْحِجِيِّ، - قَالَ مُسْلِمٌ أَبُو عُبَيْدٍ مَوْلَى سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ - عَنْ عَطَاءِ بْنِ يَزِيدَ اللَّيْثِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ مَنْ سَبَّحَ اللَّهَ فِي دُبُرِ كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ ثَلاَثًا وَثَلاَثِينَ وَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ ثَلاَثًا وَثَلاَثِينَ وَكَبَّرَ اللَّهَ ثَلاَثًا وَثَلاَثِينَ فَتِلْكَ تِسْعَةٌ وَتِسْعُونَ وَقَالَ تَمَامَ الْمِائَةِ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ غُفِرَتْ خَطَايَاهُ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ مِثْلَ زَبَدِ الْبَحْرِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏

Question: Is there a sunnah way to go to sleep, like a dua and a position?

Al-Bara' bin Azib narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said to make wudu as for prayer before going to bed, lie on the right side, and say a supplication in which you submit your face and affairs to Allah, rely on Him in hope and fear, affirm there is no refuge from Him except in Him, and declare belief in His Book and His Prophet; and if you die that night, you die upon the fitrah [tirmidhi:3574]. Abu Hurairah also reported that when going to bed one should dust the bedding with the edge of the lower garment, since one does not know what came onto it [abudawud:5050].

Question: I'm going through a really hard time. Did the Prophet have a specific dua for distress?

Yes. Ibn Abbas reported that at times of distress the Prophet ﷺ would say: La ilaha illallahu al-Azim al-Halim, la ilaha illallahu Rabbu as-samawati wal-ard wa Rabbu al-arsh al-azim [bukhari:6345]. Ibn Majah records a similar wording from Ibn Abbas that he used to say at times of distress, declaring that none is worthy of worship but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous, and glorifying the Lord of the seven heavens and the Mighty Throne [ibnmajah:3883]. Allah also says: "Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret" [quran:7:55].

Question: How do I pray istikhara and how will I know the answer, will I see a dream?

Jabir said the Prophet ﷺ taught them istikhara for every matter just as he taught them surahs of the Quran: when you intend something, pray two rak'ahs other than the obligatory prayer and then make the supplication asking Allah to choose for you by His knowledge, to decree it if it is good for your religion and life, and to turn it away if it is bad [bukhari:6382]. I'm not sure about how the answer is supposed to appear or whether dreams are involved, because this narration does not say; please ask a qualified scholar.

[abudawud:2599] Sunan Abi Dawud 2599
Grading: Sahih (Al-Albani); Sahih (Muhammad Muhyi Al-Din Abdul Hamid); Hasan Sahih (Shuaib Al Arnaut)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا الْحَسَنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّزَّاقِ، أَخْبَرَنَا ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ، أَخْبَرَنِي أَبُو الزُّبَيْرِ، أَنَّ عَلِيًّا الأَزْدِيَّ، أَخْبَرَهُ أَنَّ ابْنَ عُمَرَ عَلَّمَهُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ إِذَا اسْتَوَى عَلَى بَعِيرِهِ خَارِجًا إِلَى سَفَرٍ كَبَّرَ ثَلاَثًا ثُمَّ قَالَ ‏"‏ ‏{‏ سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ * وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ ‏}‏ اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا الْبِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَى وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَى اللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا اللَّهُمَّ اطْوِ لَنَا الْبُعْدَ اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ وَالْخَلِيفَةُ فِي الأَهْلِ وَالْمَالِ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَإِذَا رَجَعَ قَالَهُنَّ وَزَادَ فِيهِنَّ ‏"‏ آيِبُونَ تَائِبُونَ عَابِدُونَ لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَكَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَجُيُوشُهُ إِذَا عَلَوُا الثَّنَايَا كَبَّرُوا وَإِذَا هَبَطُوا سَبَّحُوا فَوُضِعَتِ الصَّلاَةُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ ‏.‏

Question: i've been making dua for years for the same thing and nothing happens. am i doing something wrong?

The Prophet ﷺ said that a person's supplication is answered as long as he is not impatient, saying that he called and was not answered [bukhari:6340]. Abu Hurairah also narrated that every supplication is answered in one of three ways: it is granted in this world, saved for the Hereafter, or sins are expiated by it, as long as one does not ask for sin or for cutting family ties and does not become hasty [tirmidhi:3604.04]. When asked what hastiness means, he said it is saying: I supplicated to Allah but He did not answer me [ibnmajah:3853].

Question: What dhikr should I do after the fard prayers?

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that whoever glorifies Allah thirty-three times after every prayer, praises Him thirty-three times, and declares His greatness thirty-three times, then completes a hundred with la ilaha illallah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahu al-mulk wa lahu al-hamd wa huwa ala kulli shay'in qadir, will have his sins forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea [muslim:1352]. Ka'b bin Ujrah also reported that whoever says these after every prayer will not be disappointed [tirmidhi:3412]. Allah says: "O ye who believe! Remember Allah with much remembrance" [quran:33:41].

Question: Any dua when leaving the house?

The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever says on leaving his house: Bismillah, tawakkaltu ala Allah, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah, it is said to him that he is sufficed and protected, and Shaitan moves away from him [tirmidhi:3426]. A different wording in Ibn Majah is graded Da'if [ibnmajah:3885].

Question: what dua do you say when starting a trip, like getting in the car

Ibn Umar reported that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat on his camel to set out on a journey, he said Allahu akbar three times, then glorified the One who made this subservient to us when we could not have done it ourselves, and affirmed that to our Lord we return [abudawud:2599]. He then asked Allah for righteousness, piety and deeds pleasing to Him on the journey, to make it easy and short, and described Allah as the Companion on the journey and the Guardian of the family left behind [abudawud:2599]. Tirmidhi records the same practice when he mounted his riding camel [tirmidhi:3447].

Question: Should I raise my hands when making dua, and wipe my face after?

The narrations point in different directions. Salman al-Farsi narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said your Lord is generous and is ashamed to turn away empty the hands of His servant when he raises them to Him [abudawud:1488]. Anas, however, said the Prophet ﷺ did not raise his hands in any supplication except when praying for rain, when he raised them so high the whiteness of his armpits showed [ibnmajah:1180]. The report that he raised his hands and then wiped his face with them is graded Da'if [abudawud:1492]. Scholars have reconciled these in different ways, so please ask a qualified scholar for guidance.

Question: What's the best form of dhikr according to the Prophet?

Jabir bin Abdullah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said the best remembrance is la ilaha illallah and the best supplication is al-hamdulillah, and Tirmidhi grades it Hasan [tirmidhi:3383]. Ibn Majah records the same words from Jabir, who heard them directly from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [ibnmajah:3800].

Question: Can you suggest duas from the Quran to make for my parents?

The Quran records Nuh's prayer: "My Lord! Forgive me and my parents and him who entereth my house believing, and believing men and believing women" [quran:71:28]. It also records Ibrahim's prayer: "Our Lord! Forgive me and my parents and believers on the day when the account is cast" [quran:14:41]. Both are supplications you can make for your parents.

Question: how much reward for reading one letter of quran

Abdullah bin Mas'ud reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said whoever recites a letter from Allah's Book gets a good deed for it, and each good deed is multiplied ten times [tirmidhi:2910]. He explained that Alif Lam Mim is not one letter; rather Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter and Mim is a letter [tirmidhi:2910].

Question: I'm a revert and my Quran reading is really slow and broken. Is it even worth it?

Yes, it is very much worth it. The Prophet ﷺ said that the one who recites the Quran and is skilled at it will be with the noble righteous scribes, while the one who exerts himself to learn it and recites it with great difficulty will have a double reward [bukhari:4937]. Tirmidhi records the same from Aishah, placing the proficient reciter with the noble and blessed angels [tirmidhi:2904]. The Prophet ﷺ also compared the one who learns the Quran to the owner of a hobbled camel: if he looks after it, he keeps it, and if he lets it go, it goes away [nasai:942].

Question: Is it good to recite Quran in a beautiful voice or is that showing off?

Reciting beautifully is praised: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said Allah does not listen to anything as He listens to a prophet reciting the Quran in a pleasant voice [bukhari:5023]. The Quran also instructs: "chant the Qur'an in measure" [quran:73:4]. The concern about showing off is a matter of intention; Allah warns against spending "only to be seen of men" and the same sincerity applies to all good deeds [quran:2:264].

Question: How often should I finish the whole quran? some people do it in 3 days

The Prophet ﷺ told Abdullah ibn Amr to complete the Quran in a month, and when he kept saying he had more strength, he reduced it to twenty days, then fifteen, then ten, then seven, telling him not to go beyond that [abudawud:1388]. In Muslim's version of the same conversation, the Prophet ﷺ began by telling him to recite the whole Quran every month and ended by telling him to recite it in seven nights and not exceed that [muslim:2732].

Question: Does reading Surah Ikhlas really equal reading a third of the Quran?

Yes, Abu Hurairah narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad is equal to a third of the Quran [tirmidhi:2899]. A narration from Ibn Abbas says the same about it, while also mentioning Idha Zulzilat as equal to half and Qul Ya Ayyuhal-Kafirun as equal to a fourth [tirmidhi:2894].

Question: What's the virtue of Surah Kahf and why is it read on Fridays?

Al-Bara' reported that a man was reciting Surah al-Kahf with his horse tied beside him when a cloud came down over him and his horse became restless; the Prophet ﷺ said it was tranquillity that had descended because of the recitation [bukhari:5011]. Abu al-Darda' narrated that whoever memorizes ten verses from the beginning of Surah al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal [abudawud:4323]. I'm not sure about the specific virtue of reading it on Friday, because these sources do not mention Friday.

[ibnkathir:56:75.3] Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Arabic) on 56:75 (part 3) (Al-Waaqia)
(ar) وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَقَسَمٌ لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عَظِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: وَإِنَّ هَذَا الْقَسَمَ الَّذِي أَقْسَمْتُ بِهِ لَقَسَمٌ عَظِيمٌ، لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ  عَظَمَتَهُ لَعَظَّمْتُمُ الْمُقْسِمَ بِهِ عَلَيْهِ، ﴿إِنَّهُ لَقُرْآنٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾ أَيْ: إِنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ الَّذِي نَزَلَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ لَكِتَابٌ عَظِيمٌ. ﴿فِي كِتَابٍ مَكْنُونٍ﴾ أَيْ: مُعَظَّمٌ فِي كِتَابٍ مُعَظَّمٍ مَحْفُوظٍ مُوَقَّرٍ.
قَالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ: حَدَّثَنِي إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ مُوسَى  ، أَخْبَرَنَا شَرِيكٌ، عَنْ حَكِيمٍ -هُوَ ابْنُ جُبَيْرٍ-عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْر، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ: ﴿لَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ قَالَ: الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي فِي السَّمَاءِ.
وَقَالَ العَوْفِيّ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ: ﴿ [لَا يَمَسُّهُ] إِلا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾  يَعْنِي: الْمَلَائِكَةَ. وَكَذَا قَالَ أَنَسٌ، وَمُجَاهِدٌ، وعِكْرِمَة، وَسَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْر، وَالضَّحَّاكُ، وَأَبُو الشَّعْثَاءِ جَابِرُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ، وَأَبُو نَهِيك، والسُّدِّيّ، وَعَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، وَغَيْرُهُمْ.

[ibnkathir:56:75.4] Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Arabic) on 56:75 (part 4) (Al-Waaqia)
(ar) وَقَالَ ابْنُ زَيْدٍ: زَعَمت كُفَّارُ قُرَيْشٍ أَنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ تَنَزَّلَتْ بِهِ الشَّيَاطِينُ، فَأَخْبَرَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى أَنَّهُ لَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلَّا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ كَمَا قَالَ: ﴿وَمَا تَنزلَتْ بِهِ الشَّيَاطِينُ. وَمَا يَنْبَغِي لَهُمْ وَمَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ. إِنَّهُمْ عَنِ السَّمْعِ لَمَعْزُولُونَ﴾ [الشعراء: ٢١٠-٢١٢] .
وَهَذَا الْقَوْلُ قَوْلٌ جَيِّدٌ، وَهُوَ لَا يَخْرُجُ عَنِ الْأَقْوَالِ الَّتِي قَبْلَهُ.
وَقَالَ الْفَرَّاءُ: لَا يَجِدُ طَعْمَهُ وَنَفْعَهُ إِلَّا مَنْ آمَنَ بِهِ.
وَقَالَ آخَرُونَ: ﴿لَا يَمَسُّهُ إِلا الْمُطَهَّرُونَ﴾ أَيْ: مِنَ الْجَنَابَةِ وَالْحَدَثِ. قَالُوا: وَلَفْظُ الْآيَةِ خَبَرٌ وَمَعْنَاهَا الطَّلَبُ، قَالُوا: وَالْمُرَادُ بِالْقُرْآنِ هَاهُنَا الْمُصْحَفُ، كَمَا رَوَى مُسْلِمٌ، عَنِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ نَهَى أَنْ يُسَافَرَ بِالْقُرْآنِ إِلَى أَرْضِ الْعَدُوِّ، مَخَافَةَ أَنْ يَنَالَهُ الْعَدُوُّ  . وَاحْتَجُّوا فِي ذَلِكَ بِمَا رَوَاهُ الْإِمَامُ مَالِكٌ فِي مُوَطَّئِهِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ حَزم: أَنَّ فِي الْكِتَابِ الَّذِي كَتَبَهُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ لِعَمْرِو بْنِ حَزْمٍ: أَلَّا يَمَسَّ الْقُرْآنَ إِلَّا طَاهِرٌ  . وَرَوَى أَبُو دَاوُدَ فِي الْمَرَاسِيلِ، مِنْ حَدِيثِ الزُّ …

Question: do I need wudu to touch the mushaf? my friend says 56:79 is only about angels

The verse says: "Which none toucheth save the purified" [quran:56:79]. Ibn Kathir explains that Ibn Abbas understood it as the Book in heaven and the purified as the angels, and he lists others who held the same view [ibnkathir:56:75.3]. He also reports that others said it means purified from janabah and hadath, that the wording is a statement carrying a command, and that what is meant here is the written copy, the mushaf [ibnkathir:56:75.4]. Jalalayn likewise reads it as a statement meaning a prohibition, referring to those who have purified themselves from hadath [jalalayn:56:79]. Since both readings appear in the tafsir, please ask a qualified scholar for a ruling.

Question: When I read an ayah of sajdah, do I have to prostrate?

Ibn Umar reported that whenever the Prophet ﷺ recited a surah containing a prostration he prostrated, and the people prostrated with him until some could not find room [bukhari:1079]. However, Umar bin al-Khattab, after prostrating one Friday, told the people the next Friday that whoever prostrates does well, yet there is no sin on the one who does not, and he did not prostrate that day [bukhari:1077]. Ibn Umar added that Allah has not made the prostration of recitation compulsory, but it may be done if one wishes [bukhari:1077].

Question: Can a woman on her period read Quran from memory or from her phone?

There is a narration attributed to the Prophet ﷺ that the menstruating woman and the junub person should not recite anything of the Quran, but it is graded Munkar and Da'if [tirmidhi:131]. Ibn Majah's version is also graded Munkar [ibnmajah:596]. A report that the Prophet ﷺ recited in all conditions except when junub is graded Da'if as well [tirmidhi:146]. I'm not sure what the ruling is, since these sources only contain weak narrations and say nothing about reciting from memory or from a phone, so please ask a qualified scholar.

Question: before i start reading quran what should i say, and how should I read it?

Allah says: "And when thou recitest the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast" [quran:16:98]. The Quran also describes itself as "a Scripture that We have revealed unto thee, full of blessing, that they may ponder its revelations, and that men of understanding may reflect" [quran:38:29]. It asks those who turn away: "Will they then not meditate on the Qur'an, or are there locks on the hearts" [quran:47:24]. So begin by seeking refuge in Allah, and read with reflection.

Question: I memorized a lot of surahs as a kid and I'm forgetting them. any hadith about this?

Yes, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that the one who learns the Quran is like the owner of a hobbled camel: if he pays attention to it he keeps it, but if he lets it loose, it goes away [nasai:942]. So the sources encourage regular revision to keep what you have memorized.

Question: which hand should i use for istinja?

Use the left hand: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that when anyone of you goes to the lavatory, he should neither touch his private part nor clean himself with his right hand [bukhari:153]. Abu Qatada's other narration gives the same instruction for when one urinates, and adds that one should not breathe into the drinking vessel [bukhari:154].

Question: How serious is it if drops of urine get on my clothes and I don't care about cleaning it?

It is taken seriously. Ibn Abbas narrated that the Prophet ﷺ passed by two graves and said both were being punished, not for something they found hard to avoid; one of them did not protect himself from his urine and the other spread slander [tirmidhi:70]. Abu Dawud records the same incident, saying one of them did not safeguard himself from urine [abudawud:20]. The Quran also commands: "Thy raiment purify" [quran:74:4].

Question: A dog drank out of my bowl, how do i clean it?

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that the purification of a vessel licked by a dog is to wash it seven times, using earth for the first washing [muslim:651]. Bukhari's narration likewise says it must be washed seven times if a dog drinks from it [bukhari:172].

Question: Is semen on clothes najis? Do I have to wash it or can I just scrape it off?

The narrations from Aishah describe two different practices. In one, she said she used to wash the traces of janabah from the Prophet's clothes, and he would go out to pray with the water spots still visible [bukhari:229]. In others, she said she used to scrape semen off the garment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [muslim:669]. Ibn Majah also reports her saying she often scraped it from his garment with her hand [ibnmajah:537]. Scholars have drawn different conclusions from these reports about whether it is impure, so please ask a qualified scholar for a ruling.

Question: How do I get period blood out of my clothes so I can pray in them?

When a woman asked about menstrual blood on clothes, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ told her to scratch it, rub it with water, sprinkle water over it, and then pray in it [nasai:293]. Aishah also described how the women, once clean, would take hold of the blood spot, rub it off, wash that part thoroughly and sprinkle water over the rest [bukhari:308].

Question: Can you explain step by step how the Prophet did ghusl after janabah?

Aishah said that the Prophet ﷺ began by washing his hands, then performed wudu as for prayer, then put his fingers in water and ran them through the roots of his hair, then poured three handfuls of water over his head, and then poured water over his whole body [bukhari:248]. Maimuna, who screened him while he bathed, described him washing his hands, pouring water from his right hand onto his left, washing his private parts, and then rubbing his hand on a wall or the earth [bukhari:281].

Question: do women have to do ghusl after a wet dream? (sorry for the question)

No need to apologise; Umm Sulaim asked the same thing, opening with the words that Allah is not shy of the truth, and the Prophet ﷺ answered that yes, a woman must perform ghusl when she sees wetness [tirmidhi:122]. Anas's narration records the same answer: if fluid is released, she should take a ghusl [nasai:195].

Question: I get a lot of pre-seminal fluid (madhi). Do I need a full ghusl every time?

No. Ali said he had a lot of madhi, and the Prophet ﷺ told him that when he sees madhi he should wash his private part and perform wudu, but if semen is ejaculated he must take a ghusl [nasai:194]. In another narration, Ali sent al-Miqdad to ask, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said the man should wash his private part and then perform wudu [nasai:439].

Question: My baby boy peed on my clothes. Do I need to wash them properly before praying?

For a nursing baby boy, the sources speak of sprinkling: the Prophet ﷺ said water should be sprinkled over the urine of a boy, while the urine of a girl should be washed [ibnmajah:525]. Aishah reported that a baby boy urinated on the Prophet ﷺ and he sprinkled water over it and did not wash it [ibnmajah:523]. When Husain urinated in his lap, he likewise said water should be sprinkled on a boy's urine [ibnmajah:522].

(en) They question thee (O Muhammad) concerning menstruation. Say: It is an illness, so let women alone at such times and go not in unto them till they are cleansed. And when they have purified themselves, then go in unto them as Allah hath enjoined upon you. Truly Allah loveth those who turn unto Him, and loveth those who have a care for cleanness

Question: I have bleeding that doesn't stop even after my period should be over. Do I pray? and do I need wudu for each prayer?

Fatimah bint Abi Hubaish told the Prophet ﷺ that she had continuous bleeding and asked whether she should leave the prayer, and he said no, that it is only from a blood vessel and is not menstruation [tirmidhi:125]. Muslim records the same answer, adding that she should leave the prayer when her menstruation comes, and when it ends, wash the blood from herself and pray [muslim:753]. I'm not sure about making wudu for each prayer in this case, since these narrations do not mention it; please ask a qualified scholar.

Question: Is it wrong to pee in a pond or still water?

Yes, Jabir reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade urinating in stagnant water [muslim:655]. Abu Hurairah's narration adds the reason in its wording: none of you should urinate in stagnant water and then wash in that same water [abudawud:69].

Question: Teaching my kids table manners the sunnah way - what did the Prophet teach about eating?

The Prophet ﷺ told the young Umar ibn Abi Salamah to come near, mention Allah's name, eat with his right hand and eat from what is next to him [abudawud:3777]. He also said to eat and drink with the right hand, because Satan eats with his left [ibnmajah:3266]. If someone forgets to say Bismillah at the start, he should say Bismillah fi awwalihi wa akhirih [ibnmajah:3264]. And he never criticized any food; he ate it if he liked it and left it if he did not [bukhari:5409].

Question: Is drinking water standing up haram? my uncle always tells me off for it

The narrations differ. Anas reported that the Prophet ﷺ forbade a man from drinking while standing [abudawud:3717]. On the other hand, Ali drank water while standing at the gate of the mosque courtyard and said that some people dislike this, but he had seen the Prophet ﷺ do as he had just done [bukhari:5615]. Scholars have understood these reports in different ways, so it is best to ask a qualified scholar how they are reconciled.

Question: is there a sunnah way of drinking water?

Anas reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ breathed three times outside the vessel while drinking and said this is more thirst-quenching, healthier and more wholesome [muslim:5287]. He also said not to breathe into the drinking vessel itself [bukhari:153]. And he instructed that one should drink with the right hand [ibnmajah:3266].

Question: Is horse meat halal? What about rabbit?

Horse meat is permitted in these sources: Jabir reported that on the day of Khaibar the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade donkey meat and allowed horse meat [bukhari:4219]. Jabir also said they ate horses and onagers that day while being forbidden domestic donkeys [nasai:4343]. I'm not sure about rabbit, because none of these sources mention it; please ask a qualified scholar.

Question: Is a dish cooked with a bit of wine okay if the alcohol cooks off? Even a tiny bit?

The Prophet ﷺ said that every intoxicant is unlawful and that whatever intoxicates in large amounts, a small amount of it is also unlawful [ibnmajah:3392]. Another narration, graded Hasan Sahih, gives the same principle about small amounts [nasai:5607]. I'm not sure how this applies once the drink has been cooked into food, since these sources do not discuss cooking; please consult a qualified scholar.

Question: I love garlic. Can I still go to the mosque after eating it, and does the same go for coming straight from smoking?

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that whoever eats garlic and onions should not come near our mosque, and that if one must eat them, they should be killed by cooking [abudawud:3827]. Muslim also records that whoever eats garlic should not come to us in our mosque [muslim:1255]. I'm not sure about smoking, because these sources only mention garlic and onions; please ask a qualified scholar.

Question: Can I eat the meat at my Christian coworker's bbq?

The Quran says: "The food of those who have received the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them" [quran:5:5]. When some people told the Prophet ﷺ that meat was brought to them and they did not know whether Allah's name had been mentioned over it, he told them to mention Allah's name over it themselves and eat [ibnmajah:3174].

Question: Is it haram for men to wear trousers below the ankles if it's not out of arrogance?

The narrations give different emphases. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reported that the believer's lower garment is to reach halfway down the leg, with no sin if it falls between that and the ankles, while what is below the ankles is in Hell, and Allah will not look at the one who trails it conceitedly [abudawud:4093]. Abu Hurairah reported simply that the part of the izar below the ankles is in the Fire [bukhari:5787]. In another narration, when Abu Bakr said one side of his izar slipped unless he watched it, the Prophet ﷺ told him he was not one of those who do it out of pride [nasai:5335]. Scholars differ on whether pride is a condition, so please ask a qualified scholar.

Question: why can women wear gold and silk but men can't?

Abu Musa reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said gold and silk have been permitted for the females of his ummah and forbidden to the males [nasai:5148]. Another narration from Abu Musa states that Allah has permitted silk and gold to the women of the ummah and forbidden them to the men [nasai:5265]. These sources give the ruling itself; they do not explain the reason behind the difference.

Question: Are tattoos haram? What about temporary henna designs on the hands?

Permanent tattooing is condemned: Ibn Umar narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said Allah's curse is on the woman who tattoos and the one who has herself tattooed, as well as the woman who lengthens hair artificially and the one who has it done [tirmidhi:2783]. Ibn Abbas also listed the woman who tattoos and the one who has it done among those cursed [abudawud:4170]. I'm not sure about henna designs, because these sources do not mention them; please ask a qualified scholar.

Question: My mom isn't Muslim. Am I still supposed to be good to her and visit her?

Yes. Asma' bint Abi Bakr said her mother came to her while still a pagan, wanting a kindness from her, and when Asma' asked whether she should keep good relations with her, the Prophet ﷺ said: yes, keep good relations with her [bukhari:2620]. The second narration of the same event, in which her mother is described as a polytheist, records the same answer [bukhari:2624].

Question: I want to go abroad for a long time to volunteer for the ummah but my parents need me at home. What's more important?

When a man asked the Prophet ﷺ for permission to go for jihad, he asked whether his parents were alive, and when the man said yes, he told him to exert himself in their service [bukhari:3004]. An-Nasa'i records the same exchange, ending with the instruction to strive for their sake [nasai:3103]. These narrations put serving one's living parents first, even ahead of a man's wish to go out for jihad.

Question: What's the reward for looking after an orphan, and how should I handle their money?

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that he and the one who looks after an orphan will be like this in Paradise, showing his index and middle fingers [bukhari:5304]. For the orphan's property, Allah says to test them until they reach marriageable age and then "deliver over unto them their fortune; and devour it not by squandering and in haste" [quran:4:6]. The same verse tells the rich guardian to abstain and the poor one to take only what is reasonable, and to have the handover witnessed [quran:4:6].

Question: How much of my wealth can I leave in my will to charity? Can I leave extra to one of my sons?

When Sa'd asked to bequeath two-thirds, then half, the Prophet ﷺ said no to both, and when he asked about one-third he said one-third is allowed, though even a third is a lot [bukhari:5659]. As for a son, Abu Hurairah heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say that Allah has given everyone with a right his due, so no bequest is made to an heir [abudawud:2870]. The Prophet ﷺ said the same in a khutbah reported by Amr bin Kharijah [nasai:3641].

Question: Do I have to give my kids equal gifts? Does a son get double what a daughter gets like inheritance?

The Prophet ﷺ required fairness: when An-Nu'man bin Bashir's father gave him a gift and asked the Prophet ﷺ to witness it, he asked whether he had given the like to all his sons, and on hearing no, he said to fear Allah and be just to your children, so the father took the gift back [bukhari:2587]. Ibn Majah records that he told him to take it back [ibnmajah:2376]. I'm not sure whether gifts to sons and daughters must be identical or follow inheritance shares, as these sources do not say.

Question: At what age should I start my kids on salah, and how do I make it fun for a 4 year old?

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to command your children to pray at seven, to discipline them for it at ten, and to separate their beds [abudawud:495]. A similar narration says to command a boy to pray at seven and discipline him for it at ten [abudawud:494]. I'm not sure about methods for a four-year-old, because these sources only give the ages; a qualified teacher or scholar can suggest approaches.

Grading: Sahih (Ahmad Muhammad Shakir); Sahih (Al-Albani); Hasan Sahih (Bashar Awad Maarouf)
(ar) حَدَّثَنَا قُتَيْبَةُ، حَدَّثَنَا بِشْرُ بْنُ الْمُفَضَّلِ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ خُثَيْمٍ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ الْبَسُوا مِنْ ثِيَابِكُمُ الْبَيَاضَ فَإِنَّهَا مِنْ خَيْرِ ثِيَابِكُمْ وَكَفِّنُوا فِيهَا مَوْتَاكُمْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ وَفِي الْبَابِ عَنْ سَمُرَةَ وَابْنِ عُمَرَ وَعَائِشَةَ ‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو عِيسَى حَدِيثُ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ حَدِيثٌ حَسَنٌ صَحِيحٌ ‏.‏ وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَسْتَحِبُّهُ أَهْلُ الْعِلْمِ ‏.‏ وَقَالَ ابْنُ الْمُبَارَكِ أَحَبُّ إِلَىَّ أَنْ يُكَفَّنَ فِي ثِيَابِهِ الَّتِي كَانَ يُصَلِّي فِيهَا ‏.‏ وَقَالَ أَحْمَدُ وَإِسْحَاقُ أَحَبُّ الثِّيَابِ إِلَيْنَا أَنْ يُكَفَّنَ فِيهَا الْبَيَاضُ وَيُسْتَحَبُّ حُسْنُ الْكَفَنِ ‏.‏

Question: How do you wash and shroud a Muslim who has died?

When one of his daughters died, the Prophet ﷺ told the women to wash her an odd number of times, three or five or more if they saw fit, with water and sidr, adding camphor in the last washing [tirmidhi:990]. Aishah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself was shrouded in three white Yemeni garments, with no shirt or turban among them [abudawud:3151]. He also said to wear white clothes, for they are among the best garments, and to shroud the dead in them [tirmidhi:994].

Question: Is it worth going to the janazah and also staying for the burial?

Yes. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said whoever attends a funeral until the prayer is offered gets one qirat of reward, and whoever stays until the burial gets two qirats, and when asked what two qirats are, he likened them to two huge mountains [bukhari:1325]. Muslim records the same reward [muslim:2189]. He also told people to hurry with the dead body, since if it was righteous they are sending it on to good [bukhari:1315].

Question: How long am I allowed to mourn my brother, and is crying allowed?

The Prophet ﷺ said it is not lawful for a Muslim woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for more than three days, except for her husband, for whom she mourns four months and ten days [bukhari:5339]. He also said that whoever slaps the cheeks, tears the clothes and calls out with the cries of the Jahiliyyah is not one of us [tirmidhi:999]. I'm not sure about crying itself, because these sources only address mourning periods and those extreme actions.

(ar) حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ، قَالَ قَرَأْتُ عَلَى ابْنِ أَبِي ذِئْبٍ عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْمَقْبُرِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ فَقَالَ سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏ حَدَّثَنَا أَحْمَدُ بْنُ شَبِيبِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ، قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي أَبِي، حَدَّثَنَا يُونُسُ، قَالَ ابْنُ شِهَابٍ وَحَدَّثَنِي عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ الأَعْرَجُ، أَنَّ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ مَنْ شَهِدَ الْجَنَازَةَ حَتَّى يُصَلِّيَ عَلَيْهَا فَلَهُ قِيرَاطٌ، وَمَنْ شَهِدَ حَتَّى تُدْفَنَ كَانَ لَهُ قِيرَاطَانِ ‏"‏‏.‏ قِيلَ وَمَا الْقِيرَاطَانِ قَالَ ‏"‏ مِثْلُ الْجَبَلَيْنِ الْعَظِيمَيْنِ ‏"‏‏.‏
